requirements.title: Expressions are formed from operands, operators, and parentheses
requirements.definition: The overall expression syntax is built from operands, operators, and parentheses. Operands are scalar or array, operations are intrinsic or defined, and an operand may itself be an expression. The detailed grammar, operator applicability, and interpretation are owned by the following subclauses.
requirements.oracle:
Future controls should use literal result checks and minimal expression shapes, while assigning actual grammar credit to the numbered rules in 10.1.2.2-10.1.2.9 and semantic credit to 10.1.3-10.1.12.

requirements.title: Expression grammar uses primary and level-1 through level-5 categories
requirements.definition: An expression is defined using the categories primary, level-1 expression, level-2 expression, level-3 expression, level-4 expression, and level-5 expression. Each category's exact syntax remains with its defining rule.
requirements.oracle:
Each future plan should name the specific defining rule for the category under observation and use an independent literal result to make the category use non-vacuous.

requirements.title: Expression categories correspond to precedence levels and bottom out at primary
requirements.definition: The expression categories are tied to operator precedence, are generally defined in terms of other categories, and have primary as the simplest form of each category. This is the structural summary for the precedence ladder, not an interpretation rule.

pending.precedence-ladder: PENDING positive-control source shapes covering the full precedence chain as separate, attributable steps: primary, defined unary, power **, multiply/divide, unary add/subtract, binary add/subtract, concatenation, one relation, .NOT., .AND., .OR., .EQV./.NEQV., and defined binary. Each statement isolates one step with a literal oracle where that step is value-observable. For intrinsic operands, grouping of associative operators such as //, .AND., and .EQV./.NEQV. is not distinguished by value; the concrete future route for those grouping facets is a non-associative defined extension of the same intrinsic-operator symbol on a derived type, with distinct literal-bearing operands and independently computed component values for the two parenthesisations. Defined-operation applicability and interpretation remain 10.1.6 and 15.4.3.4.2 dependencies.
